page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a high-density compute and memory instance hosted on KVM hypervisors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 64 shared vCPUs across 64 physical cores with single-thread-per-core mapping, supported by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. System memory is scaled to 384 GB, delivering 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage and includes no dedicated GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between aggregate multi-threaded capacity and per-core execution speed. Multi-core performance is solid, evidenced by a strong PassMark CPU rating of 60061.44, high extended instruction evaluation scores, and 400.83 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Cached memory read throughput reaches 3728.41 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core execution is constrained: stress-ng single-core performance registers in the bottom decile, while Geekbench single-core scores (1155.0) and single-threaded gzip compression remain weak. Large-block memory transfers and static web serving yield mid-tier throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared-core CPU allocation model delivers high core counts and a substantial 384 GB memory footprint at an accessible entry tier relative to dedicated bare-metal or exclusive-core instances. The primary operational trade-off is the potential for CPU scheduling contention and lower single-thread responsiveness inherent to shared compute resources. The absence of integrated local storage also requires attaching remote network volumes for persistent storage needs.

UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is appropriate for parallelized, memory-heavy workloads that tolerate shared CPU tenancy. Typical use cases include distributed caching layers such as Redis clusters, in-memory analytical pipelines, Clang software compilation, multi-threaded ETL jobs, and horizontally scaled microservices.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a high-capacity cloud server configured for memory-demanding and concurrent workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 64 shared vCPUs and 384 GB of system RAM, providing 6.0 GB of memory per core. The server operates without bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark data reveals strong multi-threaded execution and high cached memory bandwidth, highlighted by top-tier PassMark CPU metrics and parallel decompression rates. However, single-core processing metrics in Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the lower percentiles. The shared CPU allocation provides significant density and aggregated memory at an economical resource cost, balanced against lower per-thread compute predictability. The system is well configured for in-memory data processing, distributed caching, parallel CI/CD builds, and high-concurrency microservice architectures.
